materials.item: human bingo sheets (printed, or hand-drawn grids)

name: Human Bingo
safety: Roam, don't run — and only ask someone to sign if they agree to the square.
setup: Make bingo grids with prompts like 'has a pet lizard,' 'can whistle,' 'was born in another state.' Print or hand-draw one per kid.
steps: Hand out sheets and explain: find a different person for each square.
Mingle and interview: ask, listen, get a signature per matching square.
First to complete a row calls BINGO — verify by asking the signers.
Keep going until five kids have bingo, then stop.
Share-out: the most surprising signature on your sheet.
tagline: Find a different classmate for every square.

variations.easier: Three in a row wins instead of five.
variations.harder: Blackout round: fill the whole card.

name: Birthday Lineup
safety: No talking means no shouting across the room — use gestures only, and keep hands to yourself.
setup: Clear a long line of floor space. No materials at all.
steps: Challenge: line up in birthday order — January to December — without speaking.
Gestures, fingers, and mime are allowed. Writing is not.
When the line looks done, go down the row and call out birthdays to check.
Time it. Then try again and beat your record.
Debrief: what worked better than words?
tagline: Line up by birthday. No talking. Go.

variations.harder: Line up by shoe size, height, or first name — still silent.

name: Desert Island Picks
safety: Keep picks friendly — no choosing people as items, and respect every answer.
setup: Circle up. The prompt: you are stranded on a desert island and can bring three things.
steps: Each kid names their three desert island items and says why.
The group can ask one follow-up question per person.
Vote on the most practical list and the most creative list.
Twist round: now you can only bring ONE thing — what changes?
Close with the group's all-star survival kit: the best picks combined.
tagline: Three things for a desert island — defend your picks.

variations.harder: Add a constraint: nothing electronic, or everything must fit in a backpack.

materials.item: paper plates stapled to paint sticks or rulers (paddles)
a string or tape line for the net

name: Balloon Tennis
safety: Balloons pop — keep them away from faces, clear popped pieces immediately, and no running into furniture.
setup: Make paddles by stapling a paper plate to a stick. Stretch a string across the room as the net.
steps: Split into two teams on either side of the net.
Serve the balloon over the net with a paddle — no catching, only hitting.
Rally back and forth. If the balloon touches the ground, the other team scores.
First to 11 wins the game. Rotate players each game.
Tournament: winners stay on, new challengers rotate in.
tagline: Slow-motion tennis with balloons — rallies that never end.

variations.easier: No net, no scoring — just keep the balloon up together.
variations.harder: Two balloons in play at once.

name: Paper Plate Skating
safety: Hard smooth floors only — no carpet, no wet spots. Clear the area of furniture and keep a wall or chair nearby for wobbly skaters.
setup: Clear a big open space on a hard floor. Hand out two paper plates per kid.
steps: Put one plate under each foot — instant skates.
Practice gliding: push off gently and slide across the floor.
Add challenges: glide to the line, spin in place, skate backwards.
Relay: teams skate a loop and tag the next skater.
Freeze skate: when the music stops, freeze mid-glide.
tagline: Two paper plates, one slippery floor — instant indoor skating.

variations.easier: Sit-down scooting: sit on a plate and push with your hands.

name: Cup Song Circle
safety: Cups stay on the table or floor — no throwing, no stacking on heads.
setup: Sit in a circle with one plastic cup in front of each kid. Learn the rhythm together slowly.
steps: Teach the basic pattern step by step: clap, tap the cup, pass it right.
Practice slowly as a group until the pattern is smooth.
Speed up gradually — the circle keeps the beat together.
Challenge: pass the cup AND keep a steady chant or song going.
Performance round: the whole circle runs the pattern three times clean.
tagline: One cup, one rhythm, a whole circle in sync.

variations.easier: Just clap and tap — skip the passing.
variations.harder: Two cups per person, or pass in alternating directions.

materials.item: a white sheet or large paper screen
cardboard, sticks, and tape for puppets

name: Shadow Puppet Theatre
safety: Keep the light away from the sheet if it gets hot — LED flashlights are safest, and never stare into the beam.
setup: Hang a white sheet as the screen with the light behind it. Cut simple puppet shapes from cardboard and tape them to sticks.
steps: Darken the room and set the light behind the screen.
Show how shadows work: move a puppet closer for big, farther for small.
Let kids make their own puppets — animals are the easiest first try.
Each kid or pair performs a 1-minute shadow scene.
Finale: the whole group does one big shadow story together.
tagline: Cardboard, a flashlight, and a sheet — a theatre in the dark.

variations.easier: Use hands only — classic shadow animals, no puppets to build.
variations.harder: Add a narrator and sound effects crew for a full production.

materials.item: fabric glue or a low-temp glue gun

name: Sock Puppet Studio
safety: Low-temp glue guns only, and one adult runs the glue station. Buttons are a choking hazard for the youngest kids — use drawn faces for under-5s.
setup: Ask families for clean spare socks ahead of time. Set out decorating supplies and run one glue station.
steps: Pick a sock and decide your character: hero, monster, granny, alien.
Glue or draw on eyes, add yarn hair, give it a mouth.
While glue dries, write your puppet a name and one catchphrase.
Puppet introductions: each character meets the group.
Pair up and improvise a 2-minute puppet conversation.
tagline: A sock, some buttons, and a brand-new personality.

variations.easier: Markers only — draw the whole face, no gluing.
variations.harder: Write and perform a 3-minute puppet play in pairs.

materials.item: square paper (one per kid, plus extras)

name: Fortune Teller Folding
safety: Paper edges can give paper cuts — fold on the table, not in the air.
setup: Pre-cut squares of paper if the group is young. One square per kid, plus extras for mistakes.
steps: Teach the folds step by step: corners to center, flip, corners to center again.
Tuck fingers under the four flaps to open the fortune teller.
Write numbers on the outer flaps and fortunes inside.
Pair up and tell each other's fortunes: pick a number, count it out, open a flap.
Everyone writes one kind fortune and trades tellers with a friend.
tagline: The classic playground origami — fold it, fill it, tell fortunes.

variations.easier: Teacher folds along with the group, one crease at a time.
variations.harder: Theme it: fortunes about the school year, or quiz questions inside.

materials.item: found nature items: long grass, leaves, feathers, bark

name: Nature Weaving Looms
safety: Collect only what has already fallen — no picking live plants, and watch for thorns.
setup: Build a simple loom: tie four sticks into a square and string warp threads across it.
steps: Build the loom frame with sticks and string — warp threads about a finger apart.
Head out on a collection walk: gather long grass, fallen leaves, feathers, bark strips.
Weave finds over and under the warp threads, packing rows tight.
Tie off the ends and trim the frame.
Hang the finished weavings on a branch gallery.
tagline: A stick loom and a nature walk — weaving with what the ground gives you.

variations.easier: Weave on a pre-made cardboard loom instead of sticks.
variations.harder: Pattern challenge: alternate textures in repeating bands.

name: Rock Cairn Balance
safety: Small to medium rocks only — nothing you cannot lift easily. Build away from paths and take cairns down when you leave.
setup: Find a flat area with plenty of loose rocks. No materials to bring — the ground provides.
steps: Each kid gathers 5–7 flat-ish rocks of different sizes.
Start with the biggest, flattest rock as the base.
Stack slowly: feel for the balance point of each rock before letting go.
Count how many rocks your cairn holds before it topples — then rebuild.
Line the finished cairns up for a group photo, then scatter the rocks back.
tagline: Stack rocks until gravity wins — then stack them again.

variations.easier: Three rocks is a win — celebrate the mini-cairns.
variations.harder: Team towers: combine rocks into one giant group cairn.

materials.item: looped string (one per kid, about 5 feet tied in a loop)

name: String Figure Games
safety: String stays on hands — never around necks, and cut tangles instead of yanking.
setup: Pre-tie string loops (about 5 feet of string per loop). Hand one to each kid.
steps: Teach the opening: loop over thumbs and pinkies, pick up the palm strings.
Learn the cup-and-saucer figure step by step, slowly.
Pair up: one kid makes a figure, the partner 'reads' what it looks like.
Learn one transfer trick — passing the figure to a partner without dropping it.
Figure gallery: everyone shows their best figure at once.
tagline: A loop of string, ten fingers, endless figures.

variations.easier: Learn just the opening position and invent your own figures.
variations.harder: Chain figures: transfer a figure through three partners in a row.
